info.title: Kumbh Setu Lost & Found API
info.description:
Case management for missing persons, found persons, lost items, and found items at Haridwar Kumbh Mela 2027.

Staff `/api/v1` endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` except login, MFA verify-login, and refresh.

Sign-in: `POST /api/v1/auth/login` returns the token pair, or, for accounts with MFA enabled,
`{"mfa_required": true, "challenge_token", ...}` and no tokens. Then `POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify-login` with the
challenge token and the 6-digit authenticator code returns the token pair.
Citizen `/api/v1/public/*` endpoints are unauthenticated but OTP-gated where required.
Visibility for staff APIs is scoped by role and station; ids outside your scope return 404.
Errors use `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id", "details"}}`.

get.summary: Readiness: required dependencies and schema compatibility
get.description:
Required dependencies decide the status code. The malware scanner is reported but does not make the API
unready: uploads stay quarantined until it returns, and the rest of the system keeps working.
Responses name the failing check only. They never include connection strings or exception text.

post.description:
Self-register with the same exact 10-digit mobile in username and phone_number. Role is always PUBLIC
and cannot be chosen. All supplied profile fields are persisted and the existing login token pair is returned.

Step 1 of sign-in. Exchange username and password for a 15-minute access token and a rotating refresh token.

When the account has MFA enabled, no tokens and no session are issued. The answer is instead
`{"mfa_required": true, "challenge_token", "message", "challenge_expires_in"}`: show the 6-digit code input
and call POST /auth/mfa/verify-login (step 2) with the challenge token. A wrong password gives the same
`401 invalid_credentials` whether or not the account exists or uses MFA.

200.description: Either the token pair (MFA not enabled) or an MFA challenge (MFA enabled). Tell them apart by `mfa_required`.

schema.title: Response Login Api V1 Auth Login Post

post.summary: Step 2 of sign-in for MFA accounts: exchange the challenge and a 6-digit code for tokens
post.description:
Completes sign-in after POST /auth/login answered `mfa_required: true`. Returns the same token pair as a
normal login. No bearer token is needed or accepted here.

- `401 mfa_code_invalid`: wrong code (or a code already used); retry with the next code.
- `401 mfa_challenge_expired` / `401 mfa_challenge_invalid`: the challenge is expired, already used, or
  superseded by a newer login; sign in again.
- `429 mfa_attempts_exceeded`: too many wrong codes for this challenge (default 5); sign in again.
- `429 account_temporarily_locked`: wrong codes count toward the same lockout as wrong passwords.
- `429 too_many_requests`: per-IP rate limit, with `Retry-After`.

The challenge is single-use and lasts `MFA_LOGIN_CHALLENGE_TTL_SECONDS` (default 300).
Rotate the refresh token. Presenting an already-rotated token revokes the whole session.
Revoke the current session. Its access token stops working immediately.

Start TOTP enrollment (profile screen). The secret is returned once: show it as a QR code /
`otpauth://totp/...?secret=...&digits=6&period=30` for an authenticator app. Disabled (`409 mfa_disabled`)
unless MFA_MODE=totp; `409 mfa_already_enabled` once enabled.

Enable TOTP after the caller proves the current code (`422 mfa_code_invalid` otherwise). From then on
POST /auth/login answers `mfa_required: true` and sign-in needs POST /auth/mfa/verify-login. Every other
session of this user is signed out; the calling session stays signed in. This is not phishing-resistant MFA.
Change your password. Every session, including this one, is revoked; sign in again afterwards.

Email or text a one-time reset code. No sign-in needed. The answer is the same whether or not the account
exists, and the message is sent after the response, so neither content nor timing reveals which accounts
are real. Finish with POST /auth/reset-password. Returns 503 `password_reset_unavailable` only when the
deployment has neither email nor SMS delivery configured. Limited per IP and per account.

Set a new password using the code from POST /auth/forgot-password. Every session is revoked, so sign in
again afterwards. A wrong, expired, or used code is `422 invalid_reset_code`; five wrong guesses burn the
code. A weak password is `422 weak_password` and does not use up the code. Not the admin route
POST /users/{id}/reset-password.

post.description:
Files are quarantined and scanned before they can be downloaded. 201: scanned (CLEAN, or SKIPPED_DEV in
development). 202: the scanner was unavailable; the file stays QUARANTINED and is retried automatically.
422 malware_detected: the file was infected and has been deleted.
Retries are safe with Idempotency-Key or a stable client_record_id (+ device_id).

post.summary: Ask the help assistant how to use Kumbh Milan
post.description:
Staff only (`assistant:use`: help desk operators, police officers, administrators); PUBLIC accounts get 403.
Answers how-to questions about the application in English (`en`, default) or Hindi (`hi`).

The assistant answers only from reviewed help content. It cannot look up cases, people, or contact details,
and when the content does not cover a question it says it cannot confirm and points to an administrator or
help desk supervisor (`sources: []`).

- `422 validation_failed`: missing, empty, or whitespace-only `question`; more than 1000 characters;
  `locale` other than `en`/`hi`; malformed `Idempotency-Key`.
- `409 idempotency_key_reused`: the key was already used for a different question.
- `429 too_many_requests`: per-user limit (`RATE_LIMIT_ASSISTANT_PER_MINUTE`, default 20), with `Retry-After`.
- `503 assistant_unavailable`: the assistant is switched off or its language model is unreachable.

A replay of an earlier answer has the `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Optional client key (8-128 chars). A retry with the same key and question replays the answer
